source_evidence: Some financial experts advise rebalancing at regular intervals, such as every six or 12 months. Others recommend rebalancing when your holdings of an asset class increase or decrease more than a pre-set percentage.
answer: Rebalancing brings a portfolio back toward its original asset allocation when some investments grow faster than others and shift the portfolio’s mix or risk level. Two approaches are to rebalance on a regular schedule, such as every six or 12 months, or when an asset class moves beyond a preset percentage threshold. The source notes that rebalancing tends to work best when done relatively infrequently; it does not prescribe one schedule or threshold for everyone.
